title: Derived direct image and evaluation of coefficient systems
statement:
Let $u:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by small sites, meaning an adjoint pair $u^*\dashv u_*$ on sheaves with $u^*$ preserving finite limits. Let $O$ be a commutative ring, let $\lambda\in O$ be a non-zero-divisor, assume $O\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}O/(\lambda^n)$, and put $A_n=O/(\lambda^n)$. For either topos $\mathcal T$, let $\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T)$ be the abelian category whose objects are strict systems of sheaves of modules $M_n$ over the constant ring sheaf $(A_n)_{\mathcal T}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and transition maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ linear along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, and whose morphisms are compatible families of module maps. Restriction of scalars has its usual meaning [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Equivalently these are modules over the ring object $((A_n)_{\mathcal T})_n$ in the topos of inverse sequences. Exactness and the evaluation functors $e_n$ are levelwise. Use the unbounded derived categories of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the standard cohomology of complexes.

Applying $u^*$ levelwise is exact and gives $u_A^*:D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal Y))\to D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$. Levelwise $u_*$ has a total right derived functor $Ru_{A,*}$, computed by K-injective resolutions in the category of systems [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $u_A^*\dashv Ru_{A,*}$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$e_nRu_{A,*}\cong Ru_*e_n,\qquad e_nu_A^*\cong u^*e_n.$$
These comparisons intertwine the evaluated units and counits with the ordinary level adjunctions and are compatible with the quotient maps, on objects and on morphisms. Inverse image commutes with the derived changes of constant coefficient ring $-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. A complex of systems is called normalized here if every adjoint transition $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\geq n$.

Suppose additionally that for every $n$, $u^*:D^+(\mathcal Y,A_n)\to D^+(\mathcal X,A_n)$ is fully faithful, and let $M\in D^+(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$ have all evaluations in its essential image. Then the counit $u_A^*Ru_{A,*}M\to M$ is an isomorphism of derived systems; $Ru_{A,*}M$ is bounded below, and if $M$ is normalized, so is $Ru_{A,*}M$. In particular this applies to the comparison $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for finite coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison].

source.place: Construction 4.1 (printed p. 21), Lemma 4.10 and its proof (printed pp. 23–24). Final origin/normalization clause is the formal consequence of evaluation, counit, exact inverse image and derived tensor compatibility stated here.

proof.text: Choose a small presenting site $\mathcal C$ for either topos. Present its sequence topos on $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$, with the usual order on the second factor and coverings generated by covers of $\mathcal C$ at a fixed index. A sheaf is precisely a sequence of sheaves: restriction along $q\leq r$ gives its map from level $r$ to level $q$. Put the ring $A_q$ at index $q$. Modules on this small ringed site are exactly the systems in the statement; checking the sheaf condition and module operations at each index gives the equivalence, including maps. Consequently [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies. Kernels and cokernels are componentwise, so evaluation is exact. The inverse image of a geometric morphism preserves the constant ring sheaves and is exact on their modules: it preserves kernels by finite limits, and cokernels by its colimit-preserving adjunction. The level module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] respects the transition squares, hence gives $u_A^*\dashv u_{A,*}$ on systems. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to the exact inverse images and evaluations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to the additive direct images, using the K-injective resolutions just obtained, and then [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] to obtain $u_A^*\dashv Ru_{A,*}$ and $u_n^*\dashv Ru_{n,*}$ on the unbounded categories.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and paragraph before Lemma 4.10; Stacks 07A5, 079P, 070K, 015F, 09T5 and 03D7 for the generic module/derived constructions

proof.text: Fix the canonical derived adjunctions, including their units and counits, using [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy, lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. The first gives the termwise adjunction on homotopy categories; the second gives its localized Hom bijection with the following normalization. For a right resolution $s:K\to I$, a left resolution $t:P\to H$, and $f:P\to F_hI$, it sends the fraction $p_sQ'(f)Q'(t)^{-1}$ to $Q(s)^{-1}Q(a_h(f))u_t$. Here $p_s$ and $u_t$ are the right- and left-derived resolution comparisons and $a_h$ is the underived transpose on homotopy categories. Step 1 supplies the everywhere-defined derived functors for the system and level inverse-image/direct-image pairs; exact inverse image needs no left resolution. Thus their Hom bijections are obtained from the ordinary module transposes with precisely this normalization, rather than from unspecified choices of adjunction on the derived functors.

source.place: Tags 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); termwise adjunction also in the proof of 08BJ

proof.text: Use $LE_n\dashv e_n$ and its strict tensor model from [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint]. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to N$ over $A_n$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The coefficient-$A_n$ inverse image sends $P$ to a flat-term K-flat complex by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. In the two strict system complexes $u_A^*E_nP$ and $E_n(u_n^*P)$ the components above $n$ are zero, and at $q\leq n$ the tensor comparison is $u^*(P\otimes_{A_n}A_q)\cong u^*P\otimes_{A_n}A_q$. Since $A_q=A_n/\lambda^qA_n$, the term $P^r\otimes_{A_n}A_q$ is the cokernel of multiplication by $\lambda^q$ on $P^r$, and the exact inverse image of step 1 preserves this cokernel; so the degreewise comparison is already an isomorphism of sheaves before deriving. These comparisons are the canonical pullback/tensor maps of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with the second factor the constant quotient ring; they preserve its $A_q$ action. On local tensor generators the map carries $x\otimes a$ to the corresponding pulled-back generator $u^*x\otimes a$. Reducing $a$ to a lower quotient commutes with this formula. Thus the comparisons define an isomorphism of strict complexes of systems, natural in $P$ and its maps, and descend via the resolution model to $u_A^*LE_n^{\mathcal Y}\cong LE_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*$.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and the derived base-change isomorphism immediately before Lemma 4.10; Stacks 0G7E and 07A4

proof.text: For the separate coefficient-change assertion, take a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to N$ over $A_m$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Pulling back $Q$ preserves these properties by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], and tensoring $Q$ with $A_n$ computes its derived scalar extension. Exact inverse image therefore represents the left-hand side by $u_n^*(Q\otimes_{A_m}A_n)$, and the right-hand side by $u_m^*Q\otimes_{A_m}A_n$. The natural degreewise pullback/tensor map identifies these complexes as $A_n$-complexes and commutes with their differentials and maps of resolutions. It induces $u_n^*(N\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\cong u_m^*N\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ for every $m\geq n$; no flatness of $A_n$ over $A_m$ is used.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and the derived base-change isomorphism immediately before Lemma 4.10; Stacks 0G7E and 07A4

proof.text:
For $N\in D(\mathcal Y,A_n)$ and $M\in D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$, form the natural chain of bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,e_nRu_{A,*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE_n^{\mathcal Y}N,Ru_{A,*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u_A^*LE_n^{\mathcal Y}N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u_n^*N,e_nM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,Ru_{n,*}e_nM).$$
The outer evaluation adjunctions are [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint], the direct-image adjunctions were established in steps 1–2 using [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], and the middle isomorphism is step 3. The Yoneda bijection [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns this into a natural isomorphism $\beta_n:e_nRu_{A,*}\cong Ru_{n,*}e_n$. In particular this argument proves the unbounded comparison without asserting that evaluation preserves K-injectives in the varying-ring system category. The pullback comparison $e_nu_A^*\cong u_n^*e_n$ is already the termwise identity of step 1.

source.place: Lemma 4.10, equation (4.10.1), obtained by adjunction from the preceding displayed base-change isomorphism

proof.text:
Write $\eta^A,\varepsilon^A$ for the system adjunction and $\eta^n,\varepsilon^n$ for the level adjunction. The comparison of step 3 has the identity as its $n$-th component under $e_nLE_n\cong\mathrm{id}$, and hence preserves the evaluation-adjunction unit. The normalized Hom bijections in step 2 and [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint] therefore identify the Hom chain of step 5 with transposing the evaluated system counit $e_n\varepsilon^A_M$. Equivalently its Yoneda isomorphism $\beta_n$ satisfies
$$\varepsilon^n_{e_nM}\,u_n^*\beta_{n,M}=e_n\varepsilon^A_M.$$
For the unit, substitute $u_A^*H$ for $M$ in this equality and compose with $u_n^*e_n\eta^A_H$. The system triangle identity makes the result the identity of $u_n^*e_nH$. By the level adjunction, the unique map whose transpose is this identity is $\eta^n_{e_nH}$. Thus
$$\beta_{n,u_A^*H}\,e_n\eta^A_H=\eta^n_{e_nH}.$$
These are the required evaluated counit and unit identities, natural in the input derived systems.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1, adjunction mates; Stacks 0D6E for restriction/direct-image composition

proof.text:
For each quotient $A_m\to A_n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the identity topos with this structural ring map: ordinary tensor extension is left adjoint to coefficient restriction. Restriction is exact because it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Its derived functor is consequently itself by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Left derived extension exists everywhere by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives $C_{mn}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}$ on the unbounded categories. The normalization is the fraction-transpose formula of step 2. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the identity ringed topos and $u$ identifies
$$Ru_{m,*}\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}Ru_{n,*}.$$
Indeed the underlying composites of ringed-topos morphisms agree: both use $u^{-1}(A_m)\to u^{-1}(A_n)=A_n$. Thus the two possible restricted direct-image routes in a quotient square have canonically identified target coefficient categories.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1, adjunction mates; Stacks 0D6E for restriction/direct-image composition

proof.text: To check quotient compatibility, use $\sigma_{mn}:LE_nC_{mn}\to LE_m$ from [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint]. Its precomposition action is explicitly $h\mapsto t^M_{mn}\circ C_{mn}(h)$, where $t^M_{mn}$ is the adjoint transition of a system. The tensor comparison of step 3 commutes with $\sigma_{mn}$: on a common flat-term K-flat complex its components at $q\leq n$ are the pullback/tensor map on both routes, and at $q>n$ both maps have zero source. Hence the Hom chain of step 5 commutes with precomposition by $\sigma_{mn}$. Under the stated mate formula this says exactly that $\beta_m,\beta_n$ respect the transitions $M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}M_n$, with the coefficient/direct-image comparison of step 7 understood. Every Hom bijection is natural in the input derived system, so the square also commutes for every morphism of input systems. Identity and composition of quotients follow from the corresponding asserted identities for $\sigma_{mn}$; no choices of separate levelwise lifts are used.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1, adjunction mates; Stacks 0D6E for restriction/direct-image composition

proof.text: Now take $M\in D^+(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal X))$ with a uniform lower cohomological bound $a$. Both system categories are Grothendieck by their small ringed-site presentation in step 1 [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The functor $u_{A,*}$ is left exact since it is a right adjoint. Its total derived functor restricted to bounded-below complexes agrees with the bounded-below construction: a bounded-below injective resolution is K-injective [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], and hence computes that same total derived functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] to conclude $Ru_{A,*}M\in D^{\geq a}$, in particular it is bounded below. This supplies a bound for the system, rather than separate bounds depending on $n$.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), with 070K and the bounded-below injective resolution construction

proof.text: Assume the full-faithfulness and essential-image hypotheses. For a bounded-below $G\in D^+(\mathcal Y,A_n)$, full faithfulness identifies, for every bounded-below $H$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(H,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H,Ru_{n,*}u_n^*G)$ induced by the unit with the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(H,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(u_n^*H,u_n^*G)$. All these objects are bounded below by step 9 at a single level. The Yoneda bijection [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] makes the unit an isomorphism. The triangle identity then makes the counit at $u_n^*G$ the inverse of $u_n^*\eta^n_G$. Since $e_nM$ is isomorphic to some $u_n^*G$, naturality makes its counit an isomorphism too. By step 6 and $\beta_n$, every evaluation of the system counit $\varepsilon^A_M$ is therefore an isomorphism. Evaluations jointly detect derived isomorphisms: the evaluated cone is acyclic at every $n$, so the cone has every cohomology system zero, because kernels and images are levelwise. Thus $u_A^*Ru_{A,*}M\to M$ is an isomorphism of derived systems [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Formal essential-image consequence of Lemma 4.10; definition of the derived category and its levelwise cohomology

proof.text:
Set $N=Ru_{A,*}M$ and suppose $M$ normalized. Write $t_N:C_{mn}N_m\to N_n$ and $t_M:C_{mn}M_m\to M_n$ for the adjoint transitions, and write $\varepsilon_q=e_q\varepsilon^A_M$. Apply the explicit sigma-mate formula of [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint] to the derived system morphism $\varepsilon^A_M:u_A^*N\to M$. Its naturality gives
$$\varepsilon_n\circ t_{u_A^*N}=t_M\circ C_{mn}(\varepsilon_m).$$
The comparison of steps 3–4 identifies $t_{u_A^*N}$ with $u_n^*t_N$ and identifies $C_{mn}(u_m^*N_m)$ with $u_n^*C_{mn}(N_m)$. It respects sigma because its components below $n$ commute with the identity tensor maps and above $n$ have zero source, as checked in step 8. Substituting these identifications gives
$$\varepsilon_n\,u_n^*t_N=t_M\,C_{mn}(\varepsilon_m).$$
By step 10 both $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_m$ are isomorphisms; $t_M$ is an isomorphism by normalization. Consequently $u_n^*t_N$ is an isomorphism. The computation takes place in the derived categories using the sigma-mate formula, so it does not require the system counit to lift to a map between the particular K-flat representatives.

source.place: Formal normalization consequence of Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1; transition condition (4.12.2), called weak normalization in Definition 4.12; Stacks 07A4

proof.text: It remains to reflect this isomorphism even when $C_{mn}N_m$ is unbounded below. The exact functor $u_n^*$ is faithful on module sheaves: place two sheaves in degree zero, use its assumed full faithfulness on $D^+$ and the degree-zero Hom identification [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to obtain faithfulness on their module maps. In particular $u_n^*H=0$ implies that $u_n^*1_H=0$, hence $1_H=0$ and $H=0$. Exactness gives $H^i(u_n^*K)=u_n^*H^i(K)$ for every complex $K$, since kernels and images are preserved. Apply this to a cone of $t_N$. By step 11 its pulled-back cone is acyclic, so all its cohomology sheaves vanish by the preceding faithfulness argument. Therefore the original cone is acyclic and $t_N$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since this holds for every $m\geq n$, $N$ is normalized. This is a cohomology argument on arbitrary complexes and imposes no boundedness on $N_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$.

source.place: Formal normalization consequence of Lemma 4.10 and Construction 4.1; transition condition (4.12.2), called weak normalization in Definition 4.12; Stacks 07A4

proof.text: For $u=\nu_T$, the geometric morphism is the one in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. When every $A_n$ is finite, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] states exactly the required full faithfulness of $\nu_T^*$ on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$. Thus the conclusions just proved apply to bounded-below systems on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ whose evaluations are of etale origin, and to normalized ones among them. The coefficient categories agree: for a finite discrete ring $\Lambda$, the ring $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] is the sheafification of $W\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),\Lambda)$, and the inclusion of the constant presheaf $\Lambda$ into it is injective on nonempty $W$ and locally surjective, since a continuous map $|W|\to\Lambda$ has open fibres and is constant on each member of the open cover they form. Hence both presheaves have the same sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ is the constant ring sheaf $(\Lambda)_{T_{\Proet}}$ used in the statement; on $T_{\Et}$ the two definitions coincide verbatim. So the modules over $(A_n)_{T}$ in the statement are exactly the coefficient categories of the theorem.

source.place: Bounded-below finite-coefficient comparison, applied at each A_n; no claim that all pro-etale complexes are of etale origin

Removed an unused enhanced-section statement dependency; the item uses ordinary derived systems. Statement unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic module adjunction on small ringed topoi, applied levelwise; this unit has no separate underived module-adjunction theorem.
Generic K-injective computation of total right derived functors on unbounded categories, not a replacement of the six-operation route.
Generic derived adjunction for everywhere-defined total derived functors, needed for both the system and level adjunctions.
Generic K-flat pullback preservation verifies the simultaneous tensor models; no varying-system result is taken from it.
Generic derived tensor compatibility supplies coefficient pullback on unbounded complexes; this unit does not replace its ringed-topos construction.
Generic derived composition identifies coefficient restriction followed by direct image with the reverse composite.
Generic bounded-below resolution theorem identifies the D+ restriction of the already-constructed total functor.
Generic uniform lower-bound theorem applied to the system category itself.
The existing finite-level etale/pro-etale full-faithfulness theorem discharges the final specialization; it is the comparison explicitly named by the item and its ancestor.

Generic exact-functor localization identifies the termwise exact inverse images and evaluations with their everywhere-defined left and right derived functors in step 1; this does not replace the coefficient-system comparison route.
Flat-term K-flat resolution existence is needed for both unbounded tensor models, not supplied merely by the definition of K-flatness.
The explicit fraction-transpose formula fixes the canonical derived adjunction used in the evaluated unit/counit equations; it is a generic localization tool.
Passage of the module adjunction to homotopy categories supplies the underived transpose in the generic derived Hom formula.
